features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the role as building automation that multiplies limited security expertise rather than merely doing generic software work.

levels.descriptor: Shows little or no understanding of the role as a security-automation problem.
Mentions reducing manual work or scaling security in passing, but without a clear frame.
Clearly frames the work as automating security workflows or multiplying expert capacity.
Shows nuanced understanding of security automation at organizational scale, such as triage, variant analysis, or expert-capacity amplification.

features.evidence: "improvements there are inherited by every team downstream"
features.name: Platform leverage motivation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant is specifically motivated by foundational systems whose benefits compound across many teams and products.

levels.descriptor: Motivation is generic and could fit almost any software role.
Expresses interest in scale or infrastructure, but not the leverage of central platform work.
Clearly wants to work on foundational systems with broad downstream impact.
Persuasively ties personal motivation to central platform work whose improvements compound across the organization.

features.name: Developer enablement philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents security as something to embed into developers' normal workflow instead of imposing after-the-fact process.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss how security should fit into developer workflow.
Shows general interest in secure development without a clear philosophy of adoption.
Emphasizes making the secure path easier, lower-friction, or the default for developers.
Shows a strong builder-centric philosophy of embedding security into daily development through defaults, tooling, and workflow design.

features.name: Security rigor ethos
features.description: Captures whether the letter conveys a strong personal standard for building security-sensitive software carefully and responsibly.

levels.descriptor: Gives no clear signal of a personal engineering ethic around security-critical systems.
Implies care or correctness, but only indirectly.
States a clear philosophy of rigor, resilience, or seriousness about security work.
Conveys a distinctive and convincing personal ethic about holding security-sensitive systems to a higher standard.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software engineering experience the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: Captures the breadth of real product-lifecycle ownership shown through testing, maintaining, launching, or running production systems.

levels.descriptor: Provides little concrete evidence of production ownership.
Shows limited production scope, such as one or two services or narrow lifecycle ownership.
Shows several production services with meaningful testing, maintenance, and launch responsibility.
Shows repeated end-to-end ownership across many production services and launches.

features.name: Academic qualification level
features.description: Captures the strength of the formal degree background relative to the posting's minimum and preferred education.

levels.descriptor: Below bachelor's level or not clearly stated.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background.
Master's degree in a relevant technical field.
Doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central Go appears in the applicant's recent work, since the role explicitly requires Go back-end engineering.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures the extent to which the letter shows Python used for real services, tooling, and automation rather than superficial familiarity.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Python evidence.
Mentions Python as familiarity or light scripting only.
Shows substantial Python use for automation, tooling, prototypes, or services.
Presents Python as production-grade and central to services or tooling that other engineers rely on or extend.

features.evidence: "evaluation scaffolding required to deploy them responsibly"
features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has shipped AI features in production and understands the reliability work required around them.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful AI experience described.
Mentions AI interest, experimentation, or lightweight exposure only.
Describes shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality in production.
Describes shipping AI in production plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or other trust-building practices.

features.evidence: "Python agents ... Go services define their permissions and audit their actions"
features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures experience designing agent-based tooling with explicit boundaries, orchestration, and observability rather than merely mentioning AI.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based systems experience described.
Mentions agents or agentic workflows without architecture detail.
Describes building agentic tooling with a clear split between agents and supporting services.
Shows deliberate design of bounded, auditable, constrained agent systems with explicit guardrails and backend control.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience replacing manual vulnerability-report handling with workflow automation.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation described.
Mentions security automation in general, but not concrete vulnerability-report workflow ownership.
Describes automating vulnerability intake, classification, routing, or queue handling.
Shows clear ownership of triage automation with evident operational effect, such as major workload reduction or expert time returned.

features.name: Security assessment depth
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter demonstrates experience reviewing designs or code for security issues and following findings through.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment experience described.
Shows only high-level security awareness or vague review experience.
Describes conducting assessments such as threat modeling, code review, or service reviews.
Shows substantial assessment practice with clear methods, scope, attacker mindset, or remediation follow-through.

features.evidence: "turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation"
features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the applicant presents data structures and algorithms as an active engineering strength with a concrete example.

levels.descriptor: No concrete algorithmic strength shown.
Claims familiarity with data structures or algorithms without an example.
Gives a concrete example of using algorithms or data structures to improve a system.
Demonstrates strong current algorithmic judgment through a specific difficult problem and a clearly better design.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the level of externally validated security training or certification the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: No external security credential mentioned.
Only informal learning or unspecified training is evident.
Shows a baseline credential in security fundamentals, such as Security+.
Shows a rigorous practical credential, such as OSCP, or a similarly demanding hands-on certification.

features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: Captures ongoing hands-on exposure to attacker thinking through competitions or similar practical exercises.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of ongoing offensive practice.
Mentions occasional or casual exposure to attacker-oriented practice.
Shows regular participation in CTFs or comparable practical exercises.
Shows strong offensive practice with high placements or similarly credible demonstrated performance.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures whether the applicant shows public maintenance responsibility, upstream contribution habits, or user-facing ownership beyond private company work.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.evidence: "sharded time-series database / replicated cache / distributed key-value store"
features.name: Personal systems building
features.description: Captures the ambition and technical substance of independent projects used to demonstrate engineering depth outside day-job responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No independent technical project described.
Describes a small side project with limited technical ambition.
Describes a substantial personal build showing real system-design effort.
Describes an ambitious infrastructure or distributed-systems project chosen to tackle hard failure modes, recovery, or consistency problems.

features.evidence: "hours of expert attention it returned to the team"
features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter states outcomes and consequences of the work, not just the existence of the work.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists responsibilities, interests, or technologies without outcomes.
Suggests improvement, but the effect remains vague or generic.
Connects work to clear effects such as saved time, removed toil, improved trust, or better system behavior.
Consistently explains work in terms of measurable or vividly consequential outcomes.

features.name: Proofreading polish
features.description: Captures how free the letter is from distracting typos and surface errors that weaken credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent typos or malformed words distract throughout and materially undermine professionalism.
Several noticeable errors are present; the letter is readable but clearly under-polished.
Mostly clean, with only occasional minor slips.
Virtually error-free and professionally polished throughout.
